title: like and as
subtitle: like a palace / as I showed you / as a photographer
summary: Use like (= similar to) before a noun, pronoun or -ing, and as with a subject and verb (as I showed you) or to say what somebody's job or role is (as a photographer).

lesson.heading: like = similar to, the same as
lesson.text: **Like** means 'similar to' or 'the same as'. Here like is a preposition, so it is followed by a noun (like a palace), a pronoun (like this) or -ing (like walking). Sometimes like = for example; you can also use **such as**.

examples.text: What a beautiful house! It's **like a palace**.
Be careful! The floor has been polished. It's **like walking** on ice.
It's raining again. I hate weather **like this**.
'What's that noise?' 'It sounds **like a baby** crying.'
I enjoy water sports, **like** surfing, scuba diving and water-skiing. or I enjoy water sports, **such as** surfing ...

lesson.heading: as + subject + verb
lesson.text: **As** = in the same way as, in the same condition as. We use as with a subject + verb. We also use like in this way (+ subject + verb), but before a pronoun like this we can only say like. We say **as usual / as always** and **the same as**.

examples.text: I didn't move anything. I left everything **as it was**. or ... **like it was**.
You should have done it **as I showed** you. or ... **like I showed** you.
You should have done it **like this**.
You're late **as usual**.
**As always**, Nick was the first to complain.
Your phone is **the same as** mine.

lesson.heading: Other uses of as + subject + verb
lesson.text: Sometimes **as** (+ subject + verb) has other meanings, for example after do. We also say **as you know / as I said / as she expected / as I thought** etc. Like is not usual in these expressions, except with say (like I said).

examples.text: You can do **as you like**.
They did **as they promised**.
**As you know**, it's Emma's birthday next week.
Andy failed his driving test, **as he expected**.
**As I said** yesterday, I'm sure we can solve the problem. or **Like I said** yesterday ...

lesson.heading: as a taxi driver or like a taxi driver?

left.label: as + noun = in the position of
left.text: As can also be a preposition (as + noun), but the meaning is different from like: it says what somebody or something really is.
examples: **As a taxi driver**, I spend most of my working life in a car. (I am a taxi driver, it's my job.)

right.label: like + noun = similar to
right.text: Like says that somebody or something is similar to another thing, but is not really that thing.
examples: Everyone in the family wants me to drive them to places. I'm **like a taxi driver**. (I'm not a taxi driver, but I'm like one.)

lesson.heading: as (preposition) = in the position of, in the form of
lesson.text: Some more examples of **as** + noun, meaning 'in the position of' or 'in the form of'.

examples.text: Many years ago I worked **as a photographer**.
Many words, for example 'work' and 'rain', can be used **as verbs or nouns**.
London is fine **as a place** to visit, but I wouldn't like to live there.
The news of the tragedy came **as a great shock**.

lesson.text: Before a noun, ask: is it really that thing? If yes, use as (she works as a waitress). If it is only similar, use like (she swims like a fish).

exercises.prompt: What a beautiful house! It's ___ a palace.
exercises.explanation: The house is similar to a palace (it isn't really one), so we use like + noun.

exercises.statement: You should have done it as I showed you.
exercises.explanation: Correct. As + subject + verb (I showed you) = in the same way as.

exercises.statement: Do you think James looks as his father?
exercises.explanation: Do you think James looks like his father? Like (= similar to) is followed by a noun.

exercises.statement: As her mother, Katherine has a very good voice.
exercises.explanation: Like her mother, Katherine has a very good voice. Katherine is similar to her mother; she is not her mother.

exercises.statement: I prefer the room as it was, before we decorated it.
exercises.explanation: Correct. As it was = in the same condition as before (as + subject + verb).

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with the sentence that follows it.

pairs.left: I won't be able to come to the party.
pairs.right: As you know, I'll be away.

pairs.left: I'm fed up with my job.
pairs.right: As I've told you before, it's boring.
You should take more care, as I keep telling you.

pairs.left: You don't have to take my advice.
pairs.right: You can do as you like.

pairs.left: I couldn't get a seat on the train.
pairs.right: It was full, as I expected.

exercises.prompt: My feet are really cold. They're ___.
exercises.explanation: My feet are similar to blocks of ice, so like.

exercises.prompt: Marion once had a part-time job ___.
exercises.explanation: She really was a tour guide (it was her job), so as.

exercises.prompt: My brother gave me this watch ___ a long time ago.
exercises.explanation: The watch really was a birthday present (in the form of a present), so as.

exercises.prompt: He's 22 years old, but he sometimes behaves ___.
exercises.explanation: He isn't a child, but he behaves in a similar way: like a child.

exercises.prompt: Which word fits the gap: like or as?

items.text: I wish I had a car ___ yours.
Hannah has been working ___ a waitress for the last two months.
You waste a lot of time doing things ___ sitting in cafes all day.
The weather hasn't changed. It's the same ___ yesterday.
My neighbour's house is full of interesting things. It's ___ a museum.
The news that they are getting married came ___ a complete surprise to me.
Suddenly there was a terrible noise. It was ___ a bomb exploding.
Right now I'm working in a shop. It's not great, but it's OK ___ a temporary job.

exercises.prompt: We saw Kevin last night. He was very cheerful, ___ always.
exercises.explanation: We say as usual / as always.

exercises.prompt: ___ you can imagine, we were very tired after such a long journey.
exercises.explanation: As + subject + verb in expressions like as you know / as you can imagine. Like is not usual here.

exercises.prompt: In some countries in Asia, ___ Japan, Indonesia and Thailand, traffic drives on the left.
exercises.explanation: Here like = for example (such as is also possible), not as.
